articles.titulo: Characterization of Macro-Micro Heterogeneity in Shale Reservoirs Based on Full-Diameter Core CT ScanningA Case Study of Jurassic Lianggaoshan Formation Shale in Well Ping'an 3, Sichuan Basin.
articles.autores: Wang J, Gao B, … Ma Y (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Continental shale reservoirs exhibit strong vertical heterogeneity in lamellar fracture development and pore-fracture systems, yet continuous core-scale characterization remains limited. This study presents a hierarchical characterization of four Jurassic Lianggaoshan Formation intervals from Well Ping'an 3, Sichuan Basin, based on full-diameter core computed tomography (CT) scanning combined with convolutional neural network (CNN)-based image segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and pore-scale seepage simulation. The results show that (1) reservoir heterogeneity increases vertically from siltstone to shale intervals, with average lamina/interlayer volume percentages of 11.12%-12.81% and lamina densities of 130-2185 strips/m in shale intervals; (2) lamellar fractures predominantly develop along bedding interfaces, with average fracture porosity of 0.4%-0.7% and strong vertical heterogeneity; (3) within the CT resolution limit, pore-fracture seepage assemblages are classified into pore-dominated, transitional, and fracture-dominated types, with reservoir connectivity jointly influenced by fracture density, aperture, and matrix pore coupling. This study provides a continuous macro-micro integrated characterization workflow for micron-scale pore-fracture features at the CT-resolvable scale (>150 μm), bridging the gap between plug-scale microanalysis and interval-scale geological evaluation. The nanopore system requires complementary methods such as scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and mercury intrusion capillary pressure (MICP) for full characterization.

articles.titulo: [Effect of Xiongcan Yishen Formula on ferroptosis in testicular tissue of male rats with late-onset hypogonadism].
articles.autores: Peng A, Wang H, … Zeng S (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Objective To explore the effect of Xiongcan Yishen Formula on ferroptosis in testicular tissue of male rats with late-onset hypogonadism (LOH). Methods A total of 48 male Sprague-Dawley rats aged 6 months were randomly divided into model group, low-dose and high-dose Xiongcan Yishen Formula groups and propionate testosterone group, with 12 rats in each group. An additional 6 male Sprague-Dawley rats aged 8 weeks were set as the normal group. Except for the normal group, the rats were intraperitoneally injected with Cyclophosphamide at a dose of 20 mg/(kg·d) for 5 consecutive days to establish the LOH model, while the normal group received an equal volume of physiological saline for 5 days. The normal group and model group were given equal volumes of distilled water by gavage, while the low-dose and high-dose Xiongcan Yishen Formula groups were administered concentrated decoction at doses of 10.4 g and 41.6 g/kg/d respectively, and the propionate testosterone group received intramuscular injections of 5.21 mg/kg/d propionate testosterone, all for 28 consecutive days. ELISA was used to detect serum testosterone levels in rats, HE staining and transmission electron microscopy were used to observe the gross morphology of testicular tissue and the ultrastructure of Leydig cells, and RT-qPCR and Western blotting were used to detect the expression of ferroptosis-related genes and proteins in testicular tissue. Results The LOH model rats exhibited pathological changes such as atrophy of seminiferous tubules, structural disorder, and reduced spermatocytes in the lumen, as well as ultrastructural changes in Leydig cells including altered nuclear morphology, increased mitochondrial density, and reduced cristae. After intervention with Xiongcan Yishen Formula and propionate testosterone, the pathological changes in testis and the ultrastructure of Leydig cells were improved. Compared with the normal group, serum testosterone levels in the model group were significantly decreased (P<0.05), the expression of ROS, ACSL4 mRNA and protein in testicular tissue was significantly increased, while the expression of FTH1, GPX4, and SLC7A11 mRNA and protein was significantly decreased (P<0.05). Compared with the model group, serum testosterone levels in the low-dose and high-dose Xiongcan Yishen Formula groups and the propionate testosterone group were significantly increased (P<0.05), and the expression of ROS, ACSL4 mRNA and protein was significantly decreased (P<0.05); the high-dose Xiongcan Yishen Formula group showed significantly increased expression of FTH1, GPX4, and SLC7A11 mRNA and protein (P<0.05). Conclusion Ferroptosis in testicular tissue is increased in LOH rats, and Xiongcan Yishen Formula can elevate serum testosterone levels and improve pathological changes and ultrastructure in testicular tissue of LOH rats, possibly related to the inhibition of ferroptosis in testicular tissue of LOH rats.

articles.titulo: Permeability of the extracellular space in the rat, mouse, and human brain.
articles.autores: Ranjan A, Guo Y, … Boster KAS (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Brain tissue is a highly complex, heterogeneous, porous medium containing neurons, glial cells, blood vessels, and fluids. The interstitial spaces surrounding cells, referred to as the extracellular space (ECS), are critical transport pathways whose disruption is believed to play a role in neurological diseases. Therefore, understanding ECS fluid dynamics and the factors modulating flow there, such as permeability, is essential. Furthermore, because brain morphology, scale, and cellular density vary across species, understanding how permeability varies between species is critical for accurate physiological modeling.
In our study, we investigated ECS permeability by performing computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations on three-dimensional electron microscopy data from rat, mouse, and human. We artificially varied the ECS volume fraction to investigate associated permeability variations, since volume fraction changes with arousal state. We also used a mesoscale computational model to simulate the waste clearance from the brain tissue.
The mean permeabilities of the ECS in rat, mouse, and human brain tissues, averaged across sampled locations, were approximately 18, 34, and 10 nm2, respectively. We compared our computational results with those predicted by the Kozeny-Carman equation, which consistently underestimated permeability. We developed an empirical relation to describe the variation of permeability with volume fraction within the range relevant to brain tissue.
Our results show that the ECS permeability is of the same order of magnitude, approximately 10 nm2 across all species but varied several-fold across datasets. Hence, for models incorporating ECS permeability, a reasonable range of ECS permeability values for rats, mice, and humans is 10 nm2 - 100 nm2.

articles.titulo: Elucidating the Structural Features of a Class of PAMAM-Acyl Synthetic Lipid Nanoparticles.
articles.autores: Hall CB, Tan L, … Simms BL (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Herein, we characterize a class of PAMAM/acyl synthetic lipids and their self-assembled nanostructures. We explicitly determined the impact of hydrocarbon length, saturation, and synthetic lipid volume on the properties of the self-assembled, single-component nanostructure. The synthesis of the PAMAM-acyl lipid library was confirmed using nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR). Thermodynamic stability and morphological features of the LNPs were evaluated in the hydrated state using light and small-angle X-ray scattering, respectively. LNP structures were visualized using electron microscopy. The internal phase properties of the LNPs were determined using thermal analyses, showing thermal transitions dependent upon the molecular architecture of the individual lipid. PAMAM-acyl synthetic lipids exhibit a rich morphology of vesicles and micelles, with nanoparticle sizes, morphology, and bilayer arrangements that are determined primarily by the length of the acyl tail and size of the PAMAM head group. Finally, we interrogate model drug loading to envision future applications in drug delivery.

articles.titulo: Dual-Targeted Galactose-TPP Dendrimers Modulate Mitochondrial Function and Downstream Outcomes in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.autores: Jain V, Dar AI, … Sharma A (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains therapeutically challenging. Sorafenib, the standard first-line therapy for advanced HCC, suffers from poor aqueous solubility, non-specific biodistribution, dose-limiting toxicities, and the emergence of mitochondrial-mediated resistance. Here, we engineered a dual-targeted dendrimer nanoplatform that integrates hepatocyte-selective recognition with organelle-specific drug delivery. Galactose-functionalized Gal24 dendrimers were designed to engage the asialoglycoprotein receptor, while triphenylphosphonium enabled mitochondrial localization. Sorafenib was conjugated through CuAAC click chemistry to generate Gal24-TPP-Sora, which exhibited enhanced aqueous solubility, colloidal stability, and mitochondrial accumulation. In Hep3B cells, Gal24-TPP-Sora induced profound mitochondrial dysfunction, evidenced by elevated superoxide generation, ATP depletion, membrane depolarization, and enhanced apoptosis, accompanied by marked inhibition of proliferation, migration, and clonogenic survival. These effects surpassed free sorafenib and non-mitochondrial controls while preserving cytocompatibility and hemocompatibility. Collectively, this work establishes a precision nanotherapeutic strategy that couples receptor-mediated targeting with the mitochondrial intervention to potentiate sorafenib activity and overcome key therapeutic limitations in advanced HCC.

articles.titulo: Interleukin-15 complex-induced interleukin-10 acts on brain endothelial cells to reduce CD8 T-cell arrest during cerebral malaria.
articles.autores: Hildebrand JA, Lucas ED, … Hamilton SE (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cerebral malaria (CM) is a life-threatening complication of Plasmodium infection driven in part by an overwhelming inflammatory response. No clinical therapies are approved that specifically prevent immunopathology during CM. In experimental cerebral malaria (ECM), vascular endothelial cells in the mouse brain cross-present malaria antigen and upregulate adhesion molecules in response to inflammation. This causes CD8 T-cell arrest, activation, and lethal disruption of the blood-brain barrier. We previously reported that treatment with IL-15 cytokine complex (IL-15C) prevents ECM by inducing natural killer (NK) cell secretion of IL-10. To further uncover the mechanisms underlying this immunotherapy, OT-I T cells were transferred into mice, followed by infection with ovalbumin-expressing Plasmodium berghei. Using intravital microscopy, we observed major areas of OT-I arrest within the brains of untreated mice experiencing ECM. IL-15C treatment reduced the number of arresting OT-I T cells, coinciding with an increased mean velocity when compared to untreated mice. To identify the target of NK cell-secreted IL-10, we used conditional knockouts of IL-10Rα and found that protection from ECM occurs through IL-10Rα on endothelial cells and not CD8 T cells. Coinciding with this, IL-15C reduced the expression of adhesion molecules, selectins, and MHC-I on brain endothelial cells. In summary, our studies support the mechanism that IL-15C treatment reduces the number of arrested CD8 T cells along the cerebral vasculature by modulating endothelial cells to prevent ECM. These insights demonstrate the potential for treatments that reduce T-cell arrest to improve outcomes of human CM.

articles.titulo: Reactive Astrocyte-Associated IL-33 Signaling Contributes to a Protective Neuroimmune State During Chronic Toxoplasma gondii-Plasmodium berghei Coinfection.
articles.autores: Leleu I, Keswani T, … Pied S (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cerebral malaria (CM) is a lethal neuroinflammatory syndrome characterized by blood-brain barrier disruption and excessive immune-mediated neuronal damage. Astrocytes are emerging as key regulators of CNS homeostasis, yet their contribution to disease tolerance during polymicrobial infections remains poorly understood. Here, we show that chronic Toxoplasma gondii (Tg) infection protects against experimental cerebral malaria (ECM) induced by Plasmodium berghei ANKA (PbA) by establishing a regulated neuroimmune environment rather than reducing cerebral parasite burden. This protective phenotype required chronic cerebral T. gondii infection and was associated with a distinct neuroinflammatory transcriptional profile characterized by enhanced TGF-β and IL-33/ST2 expression. At the cellular level, chronic Tg infection remodeled the astrocyte compartment, generating reactive astrocytes displaying an intermediate inflammatory phenotype characterized by the co-expression of inflammatory (CXCL-10, MHC-I) and regulatory (TGF-β) markers. Reactive astrocytes represented one of the major IL-33-expressing cell populations in the brains of Tg-infected and coinfected mice and were associated with recruitment of ST2-expressing group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s), which expressed IL-5 and IL-13 in the brain. In IL-33-deficient mice, cerebral ILC2 recruitment was markedly reduced and protection against ECM was only partially maintained, indicating that the IL-33/ST2 axis contributes to, but is not solely responsible for, disease tolerance during coinfection. Our findings identify reactive astrocytes as key components of a regulated neuroimmune environment associated with protection against ECM during chronic T. gondii coinfection. These results highlight astrocyte-associated IL-33/ST2 signaling and ILC2 recruitment as components of a multicellular neuroimmune network that contribute to disease tolerance during polymicrobial CNS infections.

v6.resumo: Toxoplasma gondii crônico protege camundongos do ECM por P. berghei sem reduzir a carga parasitária cerebral: astrócitos reativos expressam IL-33, recrutam ILC2 ST2+ (IL-5/IL-13) e criam um ambiente neuroimune regulado; em knockout de IL-33 a proteção só em parte se mantém.

articles.titulo: CD8T cells induce RIPK1-regulated brain endothelial cell death in cerebral malaria.
articles.autores: Hadjilaou A, Christodoulou P, … Friese MA (39 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cerebral malaria (CM) is a potentially lethal complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection characterized by blood-brain barrier disruption and brain hemorrhage. Although immune-mediated endothelial damage is central to CM pathology, the mechanisms linking cytotoxic immune responses to endothelial injury remain unclear. Here, we show that CD8+ T cells induce receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)-regulated cell death of brain endothelial cells in mouse CM, while RIPK1 phosphorylation is increased in brain endothelial cells in human CM. Using magnetic resonance imaging, three-dimensional tissue-cleared brain imaging, cross-species pathology, endothelial translatomics, immunocerebrovascular interactomics, and genetic association testing, we identify a CD8+ T cell-dependent, RIPK1-centered mouse endothelial cell death program. Combined RIPK1 and caspase inhibition protected cross-presenting endothelial cells from CD8+ T cell-mediated death in vitro. In vivo, brain endothelial-specific genetic inactivation or systemic pharmacological inhibition of RIPK1 kinase activity prolonged survival in mouse CM without altering parasitemia. These findings support RIPK1 inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy to counter CD8+ T cell-induced endothelial death in CM.

articles.titulo: Toward More Reliable Dengue Early Warning: Bridging the Gap Between Theory and Practice.
articles.autores: Narayanasamy S, Sivagnaname Y, Krishnamurthy D (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue continues to expand globally, increasing pressure on health systems across tropical and subtropical regions. Despite advances in surveillance, data availability, and predictive modeling, early warning often remains insufficiently linked to timely public health action. The challenge, therefore, is not prediction alone but translating heterogeneous surveillance information into actionable intelligence. Key determinants, including climate, human mobility, adult female mosquito abundance, vector infection, asymptomatic infection, and population immunity, vary in feasibility, spatial and temporal resolution, and early-warning value. Climate indicators provide important context but may lack local specificity, and symptomatic case surveillance is constrained by underascertainment and reporting delays. Human mobility can improve spatial risk assessment and, in selected settings, forecasting, whereas adult mosquito surveillance provides complementary information on local vector abundance. The authors of the present study propose an Operationally Prioritized Early Warning (OPEW) framework that integrates sentinel surveillance, scale-aware interpretation of complementary signals, feasibility-based prioritization, event-triggered intensification, and explicit links between surveillance thresholds and predefined actions. The OPEW framework is not a validated prediction model but a testable operational framework that prioritizes information according to epidemiological relevance, timeliness, feasibility, and decision value. Prospective evaluation should assess predictive performance, actionable lead time, resource requirements, and public health outcomes against existing approaches.

articles.titulo: Factors Associated with Divergent Introgression Outcomes from-Based Interventions in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
articles.autores: Nelson E, Cárcamo PM, … Ko AI (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Wolbachia -based interventions were less effective in achieving introgression in Rio de Janeiro than other settings. Reduced introgression occurred in locations where dengue was historically high, raising concerns of inequity. We examined factors affecting Wolbachia introgression in Rio through trajectory modeling, spatiotemporal Bayesian models, and Ae. aegypti abundance estimation. During the intervention (2017-2020), Wolbachia introgression was 26% (median; IQR,14-44%), with four distinct trajectories. Despite receiving more releases, densely populated areas with low socioeconomic status had lower introgression. In spatiotemporally explicit multivariable regressions, higher Ae. aegypti abundance, temperature, population density and lower socioeconomic status were associated with reduced introgression. Improved characterization of Ae. aegypti abundance and other structural/environmental predictors of introgression could be used to calibrate release doses to ensure equitable benefits from Wolbachia interventions.

articles.titulo: Forecasting Culex pipiens/restuans abundance in Ontario, Canada using surveillance and weather data.
articles.autores: Li Z, Deng Z, Zhu H (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Reliable short-term forecasting of vector abundance is critical for guiding localized mosquito control, yet week-ahead prediction at the Public Health Unit (PHU) scale remains challenging. We developed and evaluated a week-ahead forecasting framework for Culex pipiens/restuans abundance using 22 years of routine surveillance and meteorological data from 34 PHUs across Ontario, Canada. Based on a subset of predictors selected through feature-selection techniques, models integrating recent mosquito abundance and lagged weather variables were evaluated with multiple regression-based approaches, including linear, neural network, and random-forest regression, under random, temporal, and spatial validation schemes. Under cross-validation, top-performing models explained approximately 69% of the variance in weekly mosquito abundance. In independent testing on 2022 to 2023 data, the best-performing model achieved a 14.4% reduction in RMSE and an absolute increase in R2 of 0.124 relative to the persistence baseline. Across validation schemes, predictive performance was driven primarily by recent mosquito abundance history, whereas recent weather conditions provided additional gains, with contributions attenuating at longer lags. Increasing predictor complexity yielded diminishing returns for week-ahead forecasting. Consistent performance across validation schemes indicates model robustness. Overall, these results demonstrate a parsimonious approach for routine short-term forecasting at the PHU scale, with potential applications in surveillance, resource allocation, and targeted mosquito control.

articles.titulo: Target and non-target activities ofessential oil, nanoemulsion, and thymol as ecofriendly sustainable tools for controlling, the main vector of lymphatic filariasis.
articles.autores: Albogami BZ, Alasmari SM, … Fadl AEA (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: There is an urgent need to seek effective, ecofriendly, and sustainable pesticides to control mosquitoes due to the rising threats of conventional mosquitocide overuse and vector-borne diseases. To achieve this, essential oil (EO) was hydrodistilled from wild thyme, Thymus serpyllum (TsEO), and profiled using GC-MS and GC-FID. Forty-nine components, amounting to 98.64%, were identified where thymol was predominant (63.84%). A stable oil/water nanoemulsion (average size 37.1 ± 2.3 nm) was produced using a green protocol and characterized. The EO (TsEO), nanoemulsion (Ts-ONE), and thymol demonstrated remarkable larvicidal, adulticidal, and repellent activities against Culex quinquefasciatus Say. Superior bioactivities were observed with Ts-ONE. The 24 h larval LC50s were 10.4 µl/L, 17.2 µl/L, and 23.9 µl/L for Ts-ONE, TsEO, and thymol, respectively. Meanwhile, LC50s against adults ranged between 9.9 and 21.5 µl/L. The lethal time (LT50) ranged between 2.1 and 3.6 h against larvae and between 0.82 and 3.3 h against adults. Botanicals significantly repelled adults at 0.45-3.6 µL/cm2 and substantially inhibited larval AChE activity (IC50s ranged between 10.08 and 25.34 mg/L). They were relatively safe for Gambusia affinis and Diplonychus indicus, two aquatic larvivorous species. Results recommend the use of T. serpyllum EO, nanoemulsion, and thymol as green mosquitocides against Cx quinquefasciatus.

articles.titulo: Using Real-Time Health Care Provider Feedback to Guide Response Efforts During a Dengue Outbreak, US Virgin Islands, 2024-2025.
articles.autores: Acevedo PK, Mac V, … Ellis EM (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: During 2024, a dengue outbreak occurred in the US Virgin Islands (USVI). To guide response efforts, we assessed health care providers' practices, experiences, and needs related to dengue diagnostics, clinical management, and reporting during the ongoing outbreak. A rapid needs assessment was conducted using semi-structured interviews with 9 clinicians across the USVI. Interview data were coded into predefined topic areas and analyzed to identify key gaps and actionable opportunities for support. Outcomes revealed gaps in clinical training, diagnostic support, and clinician-community engagement. Providers reported limited confidence in recognizing warning signs and expressed a need for additional training and decision-making tools. Findings indicated that clinicians often relied on clinical judgment for diagnosis but faced challenges related to diagnostic testing, including cost, long turnaround times, and uncertainty about test selection. Gaps in community awareness and misconceptions about dengue transmission were also identified. The rapid needs assessment was led by the Virgin Islands Department of Health and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and results informed rapid implementation of targeted interventions, including clinician training resources, expanded diagnostic testing pathways, and enhanced community outreach efforts, such as streamlined diagnostic testing processes and community outreach. This case study highlights the value of rapid assessments in guiding timely public health responses during outbreaks through provider-centered feedback.

articles.titulo: Integrated human seroprevalence study and entomological surveillance of West Nile virus in Cádiz, Spain.
articles.autores: Guillén-Calvo L, Freyre-Carrillo C, … Vázquez A (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
In Europe, West Nile virus (WNV) and Usutu virus (USUV) are emerging mosquito-borne orthoflaviviruses, which pose a growing threat to public health. Although outbreaks have been reported across the Mediterranean basin, data on population-level immunity and viral diversity in Spain remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate temporal changes in human exposure to WNV and to characterize circulating orthoflaviviruses in Cádiz, southern Spain, using an integrated seroprevalence in humans and entomological surveillance.
The study was conducted in Cádiz, a recognized area of WNV transmission, combining a human seroprevalence study with genomic surveillance in mosquitoes. Human serum samples collected in 2015 and 2022 from 10 municipalities were screened for WNV antibodies by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Positive samples were confirmed through viral neutralization tests against WNV and other related orthoflaviviruses, such as Usutu, dengue, tick-borne encephalitis and Zika viruses. Simultaneously, mosquitoes were trapped in the same region between 2022 and 2024 and analyzed by RT-PCR to detect and characterize circulating orthoflaviviruses.
Viral neutralization tests confirmed the presence of neutralizing antibodies against WNV in the local population, indicating exposure and activation of a specific immune response. We detected specific WNV antibodies in three municipalities in 2015 and nine in 2022 with seroprevalence increasing from 0.2% (2015) to 0.9% (2022). WNV-positive mosquitoes were detected in some areas, where human and animal cases have been reported. In addition, two USUV-positive mosquito pools belonging to the Africa-3 lineage were detected.
This study provides the first integrated serological and genomic evidence of WNV transmission and USUV circulation in Cádiz. The combined detection of WNV-specific antibodies in humans and viral RNA in mosquitoes confirms the endemicity of WNV, and it reveals the co-circulation with USUV, a related orthoflavivirus, described for the first time in this area. These findings highlight the importance of One Health-based surveillance programs using mosquitoes and characterizing local immune responses to better understand the orthoflavivirus transmission dynamics in endemic regions.

articles.titulo: Comprehensive profiling of genotype-specific dengue antibody responses using a newly developed single-round infectious particle panel.
articles.autores: Balingit JC, Suzuki R, … Morita K (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Neutralizing antibodies provide critical protection against dengue virus (DENV) infections. However, under certain conditions, antibodies can also enhance infection and contribute to severe disease through antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE). ADE can occur through extrinsic mechanisms, in which antibody-opsonized virions engage with Fcγ receptors (FcγRs) on target cells to facilitate increased viral entry, while intrinsic mechanisms have been proposed in which FcγR-mediated uptake triggers intracellular pathways that promote viral replication. The extensive genetic diversity of DENV further complicates the evaluation of antibody functionality, as antibodies may exhibit distinct neutralizing and enhancing activities against different viral genotypes. Here, we developed a single-round infectious particle (SRIP) panel representing 17 DENV genotypes across all four DENV serotypes. This genotype-inclusive platform enables assessment of antibody-mediated neutralization and FcγR-dependent enhancement of infection through luciferase reporter quantification. Using this panel, we evaluated antibody responses from DENV-infected individuals, healthy volunteers, and flavivirus-cross-reactive or DENV-specific monoclonal antibodies. Our findings reveal genotype-specific variations in antibody-mediated neutralization and enhancement, emphasizing the complex interplay between antibody responses and DENV genetic diversity. This SRIP panel provides a robust approach for profiling functional antibodies against genetically diverse DENV strains. While the current platform primarily quantifies extrinsic ADE, its single-round infection format and intracellular replicon-based readout provide a foundation for future investigations of intrinsic ADE mechanisms. Overall, this platform offers broad applications for studying dengue immunity, evaluating vaccine-induced antibody responses, and advancing our understanding of antibody-mediated protection and disease enhancement.
Dengue virus (DENV) comprises four serotypes and substantial genetic diversity, which can influence the ability of antibodies to neutralize or enhance infection. However, comparative assessment of antibody functionality across diverse DENV genotypes remains challenging because differences in viral genetic backgrounds can confound functional measurements. We developed a single-round infectious particle (SRIP) panel representing 17 DENV genotypes in which the prM and E structural proteins are varied on a common replicon backbone. This design provides a standardized platform for directly comparing antibody-mediated neutralization and Fcγ receptor-dependent enhancement across genetically diverse DENV strains. By characterizing antibody responses against a broad range of genotypes, the panel can reveal differences in functional antibody activity that may be overlooked when using a limited number of representative strains. The platform is therefore useful for investigating how DENV genetic diversity influences antibody-mediated protection and extrinsic antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), as well as for evaluating the breadth of antibody responses induced by infection or vaccination. Although the current platform primarily quantifies extrinsic ADE, its single-round infection format and quantitative intracellular reporter readout provide a foundation for future studies investigating intrinsic ADE in more physiologically relevant immune cell models. This genotype-inclusive panel offers a practical approach for standardized functional profiling of dengue antibodies and may facilitate improved evaluation of vaccine-induced immunity and antibody responses across the genetic diversity of DENV.

articles.titulo: CD8+ T cells and humoral immunity may mitigate the effects of antibody-dependent enhancement: implications for dengue vaccine design.
articles.autores: Drake RS, Ahmed H, … Antia R (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue vaccine development is complicated by antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE)-a phenomenon in which antibodies paradoxically boost viral growth. Signals of immune-mediated enhancement were observed in the CYD-TDV (Dengvaxia) vaccine trials, but have not yet been reported for trials of TAK-003 (Qdenga). To better understand how prior immunity influences dengue infection outcomes, we developed a mechanistic within-host model of acute dengue infection dynamics that incorporates ADE as well as humoral and CD8+ T-cell immunity. Model simulations illustrate a potentially very important difference between enhancement by antibody, enhancement by humoral immunity, and enhanced severity of secondary infection. Model results also suggest that recipients of CYD-TDV may have been more likely to experience immune-mediated enhancement because of its yellow fever virus backbone and corresponding lack of dengue-specific CD8+ T-cell epitopes. The model provides a possible explanation for differences in reported outcomes of dengue vaccine trials and suggests incorporating DENV backbones from all four serotypes as a potentially promising way forward in the design of future dengue vaccines.IMPORTANCEVaccines are typically designed to elicit humoral (antibody-mediated) immunity, and antibody titers are commonly used as correlates of protection. Because CD8+ T-cell responses are more challenging to measure, they are not typically used as correlates of protection and have received comparatively less attention. For viruses such as dengue, where antibodies may increase viral replication and thus the risk of severe disease through antibody-dependent enhancement, it is necessary to understand how humoral and cellular immunity interact during infection. Our model suggests that low antibody levels can enhance viral replication but that this effect can be mitigated by humoral and CD8+ T-cell immunity. This result offers a hypothesis to explain the observed differences in outcomes between the CYD-TDV and TAK-003 trials and suggests that evaluating CD8+ T-cell responses alongside antibody titers may be important for designing and assessing the safety and efficacy of future dengue vaccines.

articles.titulo: Insecticide resistance profile of the Anopheles gambiae s.l. mosquitoes in Nigeria: a 5-year malaria vector surveillance report.
articles.autores: Adeogun AO, Babalola AS, … Samson A (59 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Nigeria bears the highest malaria burden globally, with vector control strategies relying heavily on the use of Long-lasting Insecticidal nets (LLINs). However, the widespread emergence of insecticide resistance threatens the effectiveness of this intervention in the country. This study provides a comprehensive 5-year overview (2020-2024) of the resistance status and resistance mechanisms of Anopheles mosquitoes in Nigeria.
Immature stages of mosquitoes were collected from 72 local government areas (spanning 12 States), raised to adults and exposed to standard concentrations of permethrin, deltamethrin, alphacypermethrin, and pirimiphos-methyl insecticide papers according to WHO criteria for 5 years (2020-2024). Furthermore, molecular test and bioassays were used to determine the involvement of kdr-L995F mutation and oxidase-based metabolic enzymes in areas where resistance was confirmed. All mosquitoes tested were identified morphologically. Spatial and temporal patterns of insecticide susceptibility results were visualised using geospatial mapping tools in R (sf, tidyr, ggplot2).
Members of the Anopheles gambiae complex accounted for 95% of all mosquitoes tested across the 72 LGAs, with Anopheles coluzzii comprising 79.8% of collections. Other species encountered included An. funestus, An. pretoriensis, An. malculipalpis, and An. nilli. Widespread and persistent resistance to pyrethroid insecticides was detected throughout the study period. Mortality to permethrin remained consistently low (0-75%), indicating high levels of resistance across most locations. Resistance to deltamethrin and alphacypermethrin was also widespread but generally less pronounced, with mortality ranging from 10 to 90% and 20-80%, respectively. Temporal trends revealed localized reductions in resistance intensity between 2022 and 2023, coinciding with periods of large-scale LLINs distribution in several States. Synergist bioassays demonstrated substantial involvement of oxidase-based metabolic mechanisms, suggesting that multiple resistance mechanisms are operating across Nigeria. The frequency of the kdr-w mutation ranged from 0.0 to 0.7 and generally increased between 2021 and 2023 before declining slightly in 2024. While kdr-w frequency was significantly associated with reduced mortality to deltamethrin (τ =  - 0.179, p < 0.001), no corresponding association was observed for permethrin (τ ≈ 0, p = 0.998), and the mutation was not a significant predictor of pyrethroid mortality overall after accounting for insecticide type and spatial clustering (β = 10.50, p = 0.078). These findings indicate that the contribution of kdr-mediated resistance varies among pyrethroid compounds.
The predominance of Anopheles coluzzii in tested collections, coupled with pervasive pyrethroid resistance and widespread oxidase-based metabolic resistant mechanisms, poses significant challenges to malaria vector control efforts in Nigeria. These findings underscore the urgent need to prioritize efforts at managing metabolic resistance mechanisms through integrated vector control and further strengthen IRS with the use of non-pyrethroid insecticides. Enhanced surveillance, including molecular diagnostics and monitoring of agricultural pesticide use, will be critical for sustaining malaria control gains and informing adaptive, evidence-driven intervention planning in Nigeria.

articles.titulo: Exploring genetic variation in insecticide resistance loci in Anopheles gambiae s.l. populations from Ghana.
articles.autores: Abdulai A, Moss S, … Afrane YA (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria remains a major public health burden in Sub-Saharan Africa, with Ghana contributing significantly to global cases and deaths. Control relies heavily on vector control interventions, particularly insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) and indoor residual spraying (IRS), but their effectiveness is increasingly threatened by widespread insecticide resistance in malaria vectors. Knowledge of the molecular markers associated with resistance is important for insecticide resistance management in local vector populations. In this study, a low cost, high throughput multiplex amplicon sequencing approach was used for the molecular screening of insecticide resistance alleles in vgsc , rdl , ace1 and gste2 genes, alongside species identification and genetic diversity loci of An. gambiae s.l populations from Ghana. A total of 330 Anopheles gambiae s.l. from 18 study sites were analysed, including a subset of pyrethroid phenotyped mosquitoes. We detected 31 non-synonymous mutations in the target genes, of which 13 have been previously associated with insecticide resistance (7 in vgsc , 2 in rdl , 1 in ace1 , and 3 in gste2 ). We identified one SNP, T154S in vgsc , which was recently detected at a frequency of 24% in Anopheles populations from Guinea-Bissau. An additional 17 novel SNPs were identified, including A1553T and L1680F also in the vgsc gene. Phylogenetic and genetic analyses of ITS 2 and mitochondrial sequences showed low nucleotide diversity and limited genetic variation, indicating high gene flow across these An. gambiae s.l populations. Overall, this study demonstrates that high-throughput amplicon sequencing provides a cost-effective and scalable method for surveillance of malaria vector populations and can support improved insecticide resistance management and targeted control strategies.

articles.titulo: Dengue andexpansion into high-altitude areas of Latin America: A scoping review.
articles.autores: Chimbo-Paz BM, Acosta-España JD, Rodriguez-Morales AJ (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The geographic distribution of Aedes aegypti and dengue virus (DENV) is expanding into high-altitude, historically non-endemic ecosystems across Latin America. This scoping review synthesizes evidence on the ecological limits, thermal thresholds, and socio-environmental drivers that govern this altitudinal expansion.
Following Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, LILACS, and Web of Science through February 2026. Evidence was extracted from 28 eligible studies evaluating vector establishment, viral circulation, and environmental predictors across elevation gradients.
Synthesis confirms that Ae. aegypti has breached the historical ecological barrier of 1500 m above sea level (m.a.s.l.). Larval infestation and autochthonous viral transmission are documented above 2000 m.a.s.l., reaching established limits of 2550 m.a.s.l., with oviposition recorded up to 2900 m.a.s.l. Colonization is driven by thermal anomalies linked to El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) events, coupled with rapid urbanization and intermittent municipal water supply.
Topographies below 2500 m.a.s.l. no longer provide natural insulation against vector establishment. Public health frameworks must transition toward predictive microclimatic vector surveillance in mountain communities.

articles.titulo: Mutations in the nsP1 dodecamerization surface impair Semliki Forest virus RNA synthesis in mosquito cells.
articles.autores: Xin Q, Kavil S, … Alphey L (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Positive-sense RNA (+ssRNA) viruses remodel host membranes to form replication organelles (ROs), a process largely driven by the oligomerization of virus-encoded membrane-binding proteins. In the case of Togaviruses, non-structural protein 1 (nsP1) assembles into dodecameric rings that serve as scaffolds bridging viral replication spherules with the host plasma membrane. However, the precise role and necessity of nsP1 oligomerization in viral replication remain incompletely understood. In this study, we employed structure-based computational modeling to design nsP1 mutants predicted to disrupt monomer-monomer interactions within the dodecamer. Molecular dynamics simulations further indicated that these mutations may impair the membrane-binding affinity of nsP1. Western blotting was performed under denatured reducing conditions, and confocal microscopy was used to assess the expression levels and subcellular localization of mutant nsP1, respectively. Mutant proteins appear to not be stably retained at the plasma membrane, instead being mislocalized to endosomal compartments. Three-component trans-replicase assays and viral challenge experiments revealed that nsP1 dodecamerization-surface mutants are deficient in their ability to support viral replication. This study highlights the critical role of nsP1 dodecamerization in Togavirus replication and proposes a potential antiviral strategy targeting oligomeric protein structures in +RNA viruses.
Togaviruses are emerging arboviruses capable of causing severe disease and sporadic outbreaks. During viral replication, viral nsP1 assembles into dodecameric rings that anchor replication organelles called spherules to host membranes; however, the functional necessity of the oligomeric organization remains poorly defined. In this study, we combined structure-based modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, and cell-based assays to investigate how mutations that are predicted to destabilize nsP1 oligomers affect viral replication. We found that these mutations reduced membrane-binding affinity, altered subcellular localization, and nsP1 harboring these mutations failed to support viral RNA replication. These findings indicate that nsP1 dodecamerization is required for its stabilization on plasma membranes. More broadly, our findings suggest that targeting the oligomerization of membrane-associated replication proteins represents a viable antiviral strategy for Togaviruses and potentially other positive-sense RNA viruses.

articles.titulo: A modified vaccinia Ankara (MVA) virus vectored Zika vaccine that generates neutralising antibodies and potent T cell responses in type I interferon deficient mice.
articles.autores: Subramaniam KS, Platt G, … Turtle L (17 autores)
articles.resumo_original: To date, no vaccine has been approved against Zika virus (ZIKV). Any such vaccine must be safe to use during pregnancy and needs to consider immune interactions from prior flavivirus exposure given these viruses co-circulate and share the same mosquito vector. To address these issues, we have developed a vaccine using a modified vaccinia Ankara (MVA) virus. Here, we describe the development of this MVA vectored Zika vaccine that encodes structural proteins, premembrane and envelope, and non-structural (NS) proteins, NS3 and NS5 (MVA-ZIKA-B). A two-dose vaccination regimen with MVA-ZIKA-B resulted in significant serum neutralising activity and induced polyfunctional T cell responses that protected in a mouse model of Zika, rendering virus undetectable across multiple tissues after virus challenge. Vaccine-associated protection was also characterised by high IgG antibodies against the ZIKV envelope and potent interferon-gamma (IFNγ)-positive T cell responses when stimulated ex vivo with ZIKV peptides. Further stability studies showed that the vaccine antigens were stably expressed, and the vaccine progressed to GMP manufacturing. A phase I human trial with MVA-ZIKA-B is ongoing.

articles.titulo: Multidimensional behavioral signatures of Culex quinquefasciatus (Diptera: Culicidae) in response to botanical volatiles reveal divergent patterns of mosquito displacement and behavioral disturbance.
articles.autores: Chandrasegaran K, Cannell E, … Gerry AC (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Underground storm drain systems (USDS) are productive but under-targeted habitats for Culex quinquefasciatus, where high organic loads, insecticide resistance, and odor-rich conditions complicate mosquito control. Spatial repellents offer a promising alternative, yet "repellency" encompasses multiple behavioral modes that remain poorly resolved for botanical volatiles. Here, we evaluated 4 individual plant-derived compounds, 2 whole essential oils, selected vapor-phase mixtures, and USDS water odors using a modified excito-repellency chamber to quantify escape, flying, and walking behaviors in Cx. quinquefasciatus. Botanical oils produced distinct, time-dependent behavioral profiles. Eugenol, citronellol, and geraniol primarily elicited escape-dominant responses consistent with spatial repellency, whereas flight activity under peppermint oil varied with active tube exposure level and time, and was accompanied by comparatively weaker escape responses. Mixture responses generally resembled the behavioral profile of the more strongly represented component rather than showing a clearly intermediate pattern. Joint escape-flight trajectories showed that treatments also differed in the temporal organization of these responses, ranging from rapid, sustained displacement to early within-chamber activation followed by delayed escape. Sewer water odors attenuated the magnitude of escape and flight responses but preserved the relative ordering of treatment-specific behavioral profiles. These findings demonstrate that botanical volatiles can produce distinct behavioral response profiles that remain detectable in a chemically complex odor environment. By repeatedly quantifying escape, flight, and walking activity within a single experimental system, this study provides a comparative behavioral framework to identify volatile treatments that warrant further evaluation to alter adult mosquito retention in odor-rich urban infrastructures, such as underground storm drains.

articles.titulo: Sublethal costs of infection reduce performance of collective tasks in social insects: a modelling study.
articles.autores: Rajagopal S, Sasaki T, Hall RJ (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Group living confers benefits such as improved foraging efficiency, but social insects also face costs, including increased risk of parasitism. Infection can alter individual and social behaviours, potentially reducing the performance of collective tasks through impaired individual performance, reduced recruitment, and disrupted information transfer. Alternatively, interactions with uninfected groupmates may buffer these effects by facilitating social learning. However, we lack a mechanistic framework for quantifying how infection influences collective behaviours through direct and socially mediated effects. We developed an agent-based model, parameterized for the ant Temnothorax rugatulus, to investigate how infection influences collective foraging. We varied the magnitude of behavioural costs and infection prevalence and recorded effects on colony performance and reciprocal effects of infected individuals on uninfected individuals (and vice-versa). Individual-level behavioural costs had the greatest impact on collective performance when they occurred early in the foraging process, while reduced recruitment further amplified these effects. We also found reciprocal effects between infected and uninfected ants that scale with infection prevalence, suggesting social interactions can buffer declines in colony performance only when infection levels are low. Our study provides a mechanistic understanding of how infection-related changes in behaviour can impact groups, with important consequences for fitness of group-living insects.

articles.titulo: Mosquito Surveillance in Quarantine Areas of Ports and Airports in the Chungcheong Region, Republic of Korea, 2025.
articles.autores: Lim B, Yoon Y, … Jeon JH (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
To investigate mosquito species composition and mosquito-borne pathogens in airport and seaport quarantine areas in the Chungcheong region to support the prevention of imported vectors and mosquito-borne diseases.
Mosquitoes were collected twice monthly from March to November 2025 at nine sites in Gunsan Port, Pyeongtaek-Dangjin Port, Daesan Port, and Cheongju International Airport, using black light, Biogents-sentinel, and gravid traps, except once in March and November. Collected mosquitoes were identified and subsequently tested for flaviviruses and chikungunya virus using nucleic acid detection assays.
A total of 8,393 mosquitoes representing nine species were collected. Culex pipiens predominated (67.3%), followed by Aedes albopictus (16.9%), Aedes vexans (4.0%), Anopheles spp. (3.4%), and Ochlerotatus koreicus (2.8%). Mosquito abundance peaked in July, with Gunsan Port accounting for 58.8% of all collections. All mosquito pools tested negative for flavivirus and chikungunya virus.
No exotic mosquito species, including Aedes aegypti, or mosquito-borne pathogens were detected in the quarantine zones. However, Cx. pipiens, a potential vector of West Nile virus, and Ae. albopictus, a potential vector of dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses, increased by 152.7% and 52.3%, respectively, compared with the previous year (2,235 and 929, respectively). Continued mosquito vector surveillance in quarantine areas can provide baseline data to support for early detection of introduced mosquito-borne disease risks and inform effective quarantine and vector control strategies.

articles.titulo: Spatial isotope tracing maps compartmentalized nutrient use across the adult fruit fly.
articles.autores: Moon SJ, Huang K, … Perrimon N (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Drosophila melanogaster is a powerful model for studying systemic metabolism. Although metabolism is compartmentalized across tissues, prior work in adult Drosophila has mostly measured it in dissected tissues rather than in situ , limiting the spatial information that can be gained. Here, we combine whole-fly massspectrometry imaging with stable-isotope tracing and flux modeling to quantify metabolic activities across the adult fruit fly in a spatially resolved manner. Across 68 tracer-fed Oregon-R female flies and 187,709 pixels, we map 81 metabolites onto eight annotated regions, including muscle, fat body, gut, and nervous system. Glucose labeling and fitted relative fluxes indicate higher glycolytic and tricarboxylic acid cycle turnover in thoracic muscle than in abdominal fat body; proline labels the nervous system and eye; glutamine the abdominal reproductive system and gut. Alanine carries glucose-derived carbon through the hemolymph and transfers nitrogen into glutamate. In flies bearing yorkie-driven gut tumors, alanine contribution to malate rises in gut and abdomen, and reducing gut alanine uptake lowers tumor burden. Together, this work establishes a framework for quantitative spatial metabolic analysis, showing compartmentalized nutrient use across the adult fruit fly.
